_note: 006-async-mutex T071 baseline — MEASURED on linux-clang-release (2026-05-19). METHODOLOGY: these are END-TO-END per-operation wall times of the coroutine + asio io_context round-trip (manual-timed, warm cache), NOT isolated-primitive micro-latencies. Every async_lock necessarily traverses asio::async_initiate + an io_context turn, so the absolute figures sit ABOVE the [2f §6.3] isolated-CAS ceilings (which describe the primitive's own instruction cost, ~ns). This is expected and acceptable: the ±5% regression gate is SOFT and currently DISABLED per [const §VIII.2] (becomes hard only once Phase 4 module 1 closes). These measured_ns are the regression anchor for future end-to-end ±5% comparison via tools/bench_compare.py; the ceiling_ns/ceiling_source fields are retained as the [2f §6.3] design references (not a hard gate here). Drain-side / cancel_and_drain rows remain bench-harness-soft per [2e §6.6].

context.measurement: end-to-end coroutine + io_context, manual_time, warm cache, periodic post-trampoline to bound asio inline-resume recursion

benchmarks.name: BM_AsyncMutex_AsyncLock_Uncontended
benchmarks.ceiling_source: [2f §6.3 row 1]: async_lock uncontended, single CAS fast path, <= 20-25 ns (isolated primitive)

benchmarks.name: BM_AsyncMutex_Unlock_Uncontended
benchmarks.ceiling_source: [2f §6.3 row 3]: unlock uncontended, empty LIFO, <= 15 ns (isolated primitive)

benchmarks.name: BM_AsyncMutex_AsyncLock_Contended
benchmarks.ceiling_source: [2f §6.3 row 2]: async_lock contended (waiter suspends), LIFO push + slot bind, <= 80 ns (isolated primitive)

benchmarks.name: BM_AsyncMutex_DispatchVsPost_Delta
benchmarks.ceiling_source: [2f §6.3 / §4.6]: dispatch ~ 0 ns extra; post ~ 25 ns extra. Post-Erratum-E-3 both policies post for waiter resumption, so the delta is ~ 0 (measured noise).
